title: the Yaksha's questions
hook: a deer runs off with a brahmin's fire-sticks, the brothers chase it into thirst, and a voice at a lake says: answer first

segments.voice: Yesterday, Savitri and Satyavan came home through the dark, and Markandeya told Yudhishthira that Draupadi would save them all. Your line was Savitri and Satyavan. Who did you tell you were glad they're here? Day eight hundred one.

A pair of fire-sticks, swinging from a deer's antlers. A brahmin comes running to the Pandavas in their forest exile. He had left his arani, the two pieces of wood he rubs together to kindle his sacred fire, hanging on a tree. A deer came by, rubbed against the tree, and the sticks caught in its antlers. Now it's bounding away with them. Without them, he can't keep his fire. The five brothers take up their bows and go after it, deeper into the trees than any of them meant to go.
screen: `FIRE-STICKS ON A DEER'S ANTLERS.` → `A BRAHMIN'S FIRE AT STAKE.` → `FIVE BROTHERS GIVE CHASE.`

segments.voice: The deer stays just out of reach. The brothers shoot and miss, chase and fall behind, and then it's simply gone. They sink down under a tree, exhausted and parched. And in that low moment the talk turns sour. Nakula asks why trouble keeps finding a family that has tried to live rightly. One by one the brothers remember the dice hall and what they failed to do there. Yudhishthira says only that misfortune has no limits, and no one can say where it comes from. Then he turns practical. Nakula, he says, climb that tree and look for water. Nakula climbs and sees green plants and cranes, the signs of water not far off. He goes alone, to bring some back. He finds a lake, clear and still. He is about to drink when a voice speaks from nowhere. Don't be rash, child. This lake is mine. Answer my questions first, then drink and take as much as you like. Nakula is burning with thirst. He doesn't stop. He kneels, drinks, and falls down dead on the bank. So the episode begins, not with a riddle, but with a duty: a brother running after someone else's fire. And it reaches its crisis with a plain temptation, water to a thirsty man, and one voice asking him to pause first. The questions haven't been asked yet. Today, only the door: the lake, the voice, and a brother who didn't wait to hear them.
screen: `A CHASE THAT COMES TO NOTHING.` · `NAKULA CLIMBS AND SEES CRANES.` · `THIS LAKE IS MINE. ANSWER FIRST.` · then, large: `HE DRINKS, AND FALLS.`

segments.voice: Settle, and let the breath come and go. If there's a glass of water near you, set it where you can see it. If not, picture one. Let it wait there, the way the lake waited in front of Nakula. Ask yourself one plain question: what do I actually need right now? Don't hurry the answer. Breathe in, and ask. Breathe out, and listen. When the bell rings, drink slowly, if you like. If you pray, you can offer that pause in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
The Yaksha's questions. A voice at a lake that asks before it lets anyone drink, and a brother too thirsty to listen. Today's words.
Your line: the Yaksha's questions. Today, before your first drink of water, stop and ask yourself one honest question. Day eight hundred one.

howItsDone: The Yaksha's questions are a dialogue on dharma set in the Pandavas' forest years, and the episode opens with the brothers' chase to recover a brahmin's fire-sticks.

original.note: Sanskrit: arani, the fire-sticks rubbed together to kindle a sacred fire.

trapdoor: what you thought: a riddle contest at a lake.
what it means: it starts with a duty, chasing a brahmin's stolen fire-sticks, and a brother who drinks before he listens.
what a scholar hears: arani, the wooden fire-drill of the Vedic fire. the whole episode is set going by someone else's fire.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parva), the episode of the Yaksha's questions: the brahmin's arani carried off by a deer; the chase; the brothers' talk under the tree; Nakula at the lake

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: the brahmin's arani hung on a tree and caught in a deer's antlers; the chase fails; under the tree Nakula asks why misfortune comes to the virtuous, and the brothers recall the dice hall; Yudhishthira's reply on misfortune.
Confirm Nakula climbs a tree and sees water plants and cranes, and the voice's words (the lake is mine; answer first, then drink and take).
Original: अरणि; confirm spelling and stress. Some editions call the episode Aranya rather than Vana Parva.
